title: Separate data-source health alerts from app-specific execution-error handling
answers: Why am I getting noisy DatasourceError alerts on my dashboard alert rules?
How do I stop transient data source blips from firing alongside my real alert condition?
How should I set up an alert specifically for data source unavailability?
What should 'Alert state if execution error or timeout' be set to?
body:
Symptom: customers see noisy `DatasourceError` alerts fire on application-specific alert rules whenever the queried data source has a brief, transient connectivity issue.
Root cause: those rules have 'Alert state if execution error or timeout' set to Alerting, so any transient query failure fires the rule, conflated with the real condition being monitored.
Fix pattern (config, not code): set that option to Normal or Keep Last State on application-specific rules, and instead build one dedicated rule per data source that reuses a cheap, reliable query, sets the same option to Alerting, and adds a pending period (e.g. 5m) so it only fires on sustained unavailability.
Constraints: applies to any data source type, including Prometheus-style ones — `up`/`probe_success` only detect target-level unreachability via a query, not data-source-level outages; data-source unreachability is always detected via execution-error handling, not a metric query. Decide the per-rule setting individually, based on whether a dedicated connectivity alert already covers that data source.
applies: Grafana Alerting rule configuration guidance; any alert rule whose data source may become transiently unreachable.
